title: Count Pairs Whose Sum is Less than Target
summary: Given an array of integers indexed from 0 to n-1 and a target integer, count the number of unique pairs (i, j) such that i is less than j and the sum of the elements at these indices is less than the target.
statement: Given an array of integers indexed from 0 to n-1 and a target integer, count the number of unique pairs (i, j) such that i is less than j and the sum of the elements at these indices is less than the target.
constraints: Count index pairs i,j with i less than j.
A pair qualifies only when nums[i]+nums[j] is strictly less than target.
Return the total number of qualifying pairs, including pairs formed by equal values at different indices.
hints: Sort a copy so pair sums change monotonically.
If the two endpoints are too large, decrease the right endpoint.
If they qualify, the left value also qualifies with every index through right, adding right-left pairs at once.
Sorting preserves values and multiplicities; monotonicity proves every pair is counted once without checking it individually.
editorial: Sorting preserves values and multiplicities; monotonicity proves every pair is counted once without checking it individually.

tests.explanation: Exactly three pairs use -1 with either one or with two.
Ten distinct index pairs have sums strictly below negative two.
